sections.heading: Stack Definition
points: A stack is a LIFO (last in, first out) data structure.
It can be thought of as a pile of plates.
Elements are added and removed from the top.
All stack operations have an average time complexity of O(1).

sections.heading: Stack Operations
points: push(x) adds an element to the top of the stack.
pop() removes the top element from the stack.
peek() reads the top element without removing it.
All stack operations have an average time complexity of O(1).

sections.heading: Stack Implementations
points: Array-based stack: uses an array and a top index.
Linked stack: uses dynamic memory allocation and a pointer to the top node.
Array-based stack has a fixed capacity, while linked stack has no fixed capacity.
push operation increments the top index in array-based stack.

sections.heading: Uses of Stacks
points: Undo history: stacks can be used to implement undo functionality.
Call stack: stacks are used to manage function calls in a program.
Balanced brackets: stacks can be used to check if brackets in an expression are balanced.
DFS: stacks can be used to implement depth-first search in a graph.

sections.heading: Balanced Brackets
points: Push every opening bracket onto the stack.
When a closing bracket is encountered, pop the corresponding opening bracket from the stack.
Compare the popped opening bracket with the closing bracket.
If they match, the brackets are balanced.
